Subject: Observability add-ons: storage & tracing alignment + flex credit request

Hi Sandeep —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Per our conversation, I’m attaching a short outline that calls out three ways GrayLine could consume the observability add-ons (retention storage, tracing, advanced dashboards):

- Seat-based add-on (classic): per-seat dashboard entitlements + per-GB retention surcharge
- Seatless (ingest-metered): ingest-first pricing with flex credits to smooth volume spikes
- Hybrid commit: annual storage reservation + lower trace egress rate

Attachment: obs_pricing_outline_v1.pdf (one-page summary)

Two asks from our side to help finalize commercial terms:
1) Which of the three models aligns best with your procurement priorities (predictability vs. cost-for-volume)?
2) Would GrayLine consider a 12-month storage commit (pilot-level) in exchange for a usage credit pool we apply against trace egress overage?

If you’re good with it, I’ll loop in Lauren (pricing/legal) and Neha (renewals/SA) to draft a small SOW and sample invoice.

Best,

Appreciate the clear summary. Short answers:

3) Can you provide an example monthly invoice that shows credits applied to trace egress?

Procurement is looped here — they’ll want a line itemized SOW and a clear concession if there’s a discount for a 12-month commit.

Sandeep —

Quick answers inline, and a proposed commercial structure beneath: 

1) Flex credits: credits are purchased as part of an annual commit and top up a pool that applies to trace egress and burst retention. Unused credits roll forward for one quarter, then expire. Credits are applied after we invoice usage.

2) Hybrid commit minimum: for pilot-level commitments we typically accept a $25k annual storage reservation (3–6 months ramp expected). That buys a 10% discount on trace egress and a 15% applicative credit against retention overages.

3) Example invoice: attaching a sample SOW + sample invoice that shows credits line-itemed (SOW_GrayLine_202805.pdf).

Proposed pricing (pilot):
- Seatless ingest-metered baseline: $0.035 per ingested GB (first 50TB)
- Annual storage reservation (optional): $25,000 -> applies 15% credit to retention overage, 10% discount on trace egress
- Flex credits pool: $8,000 upfront (applies to egress/retention spikes; roll-forward for one quarter)

Concession: If GrayLine signs the 12-month hybrid commit, Redwood can extend a one-time 20% concession on the flex credits pool (i.e., $8k price -> $6.4k). This is a negotiable one-time concession we can document in the SOW.

If that structure looks reasonable I’ll coordinate with Lauren on contract language (SLA exceptions for retention durability) and with Neha on how this maps to renewal mechanics.

Would you be open to a short call tomorrow for procurement to walk through the sample invoice?

Best,
Ben

--

Subject: RE: Observability add-ons: storage & tracing alignment + flex credit request

Thanks for the context, Ben. I reviewed the pilot concession andthe proposed 20% one-time concession on the flex credit pool is acceptable from a pricing delegation standpoint for pilot deals up to $35k TCV. A couple of legal/ops notes we should surface to GrayLine before finalizing the SOW:

- Credit expiry: confirm the one-quarter roll-forward and include explicit examples in the SOW; operations will need a clear reconciliation window.
- Data retention SLA: we should map retention tiers to recovery windows (30/90/365 days) and any archival export fees.
- Invoicing cadence: clarify whether credits are invoiced upfront (recommended) vs applied retroactively; if retrospective, include a monthly reconciliation clause.

Ben — happy to jump on the procurement call. I’m fine approving the 20% concession for this pilot; please document the concession line in the SOW and route the draft to legal for a quick redline. Neha, can you confirm how this will show up in renewal modeling?

Lauren Bishop
Head of Commercial Operations, Redwood Inference
